CVE-2024-6763 affects Jetty's HttpURI authority parsing. The fix requires Jetty 12.0.12, a major version jump from the current 9.4.58. Upgrading to Jetty 12.x would require significant code changes in Data Prepper's HTTP handling and is not feasible for a patch release. The vulnerability requires an application to use HttpURI as a validation utility and pass decoded user data as an encoded URI, which is not a pattern used in Data Prepper's codebase. Data Prepper's HTTP server uses com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer for the management API, not Jetty's HttpURI for URI validation. Investigation ongoing for a backport or alternative mitigation.

Verified: the CVE is HTTP Request/Response Smuggling in jetty-http's server-side HTTP request parser. Data Prepper's management HTTP server is com.sun.net.httpserver (jdk-builtin), not jetty — verified by string-scanning the compiled DataPrepperServer.class: only Lcom/sun/net/httpserver/HttpServer references appear, no Lorg/eclipse/jetty/server/ references. The bundled jetty-http jar is pulled transitively by five other jars (hadoop-common, micrometer-core, spring-web, websocket-client, zookeeper), and in every case as an HTTP **client**, not a server: micrometer-core scrapes metrics from external jetty services, spring-web's embedded-jetty scaffolding is not wired in (Spring Boot embedded server is not used; the management API is jdk-builtin), websocket-client is by name a client, and hadoop-common / zookeeper jetty servers run as internal hadoop/zk services that data-prepper-as-a-client doesn't expose. The vulnerable server-side request parser is not on any code path data-prepper exercises. Even when an operator opts in to a plugin that fronts HTTP traffic, those plugins use armeria-netty (otel_trace_source), not jetty. There is no upstream binary to bump to (jetty-9.4.60 is neither on Maven Central nor in the jetty.project git repo as of the scan date — the advisory's 'Fixed: 9.4.60' is aspirational; 9.4 is end-of-community-support).

HTTP/1.1 chunked-extension request smuggling in Jetty. Fix is published only in Jetty 9.4.60 (HeroDevs commercial extended-support backport); no public OSS release exists on the 9.4.x line. Upstream Apache ZooKeeper 3.8.6 and 3.9.5 still pin jetty.version=9.4.58.v20250814. Mitigation requires either a HeroDevs-licensed jetty-http or a major-version bump to Jetty 10/11/12 (jakarta.servlet API), neither of which is currently validated for ZooKeeper's admin server.
